Logical quality | In many philosophies of logic statements are categorized into different logical qualities based on how they go about saying what they say.  Doctrines of logical quality are an attempt to answer the question: “How many qualitatively different ways are there of saying something?”  Aristotle answers, two: you can affirm something of something or deny something of something.  Since Frege, the normal answer in the West, is only one, assertion, but what is said, the content of the claim, can vary.
